newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia coal union demands cannot be met - PW.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia coal union demands cannot be met - PW.

text.p: The administrators of Metropolitan Colliery Ltd did not have the cash available to pay full severance and retrenchment entitlements to sacked miners despite a threatened Australian national coal strike, Price Waterhouse administrator Nick Brooke told Reuters.

Brooke was speaking soon after Construction Forestry Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) general president John Maitland issued a statement that a national coal strike would be called from early next month unless 137 workers retrenched from Metropolitan Colliery received full severance and retrenchment entitlements.
Maitland gave a December 11 deadline for payment.

Brooke, appointed administrator on October 29 to the Denehurst Ltd-owned colliery, said employees had been told that about A$700,000 was available to pay a pro rata proportion of their entitlements totalling A$4.9 million.
Some of this was paid last week and the balance would be paid this week, he said.
Any further funds would be subject to sale of the mine, which was "some way down the track", potentially up to six months away, he said.
It would also depend on support from the two secured creditors, he said.

The first ranking fixed-charge creditor was Japanese trading house Kanematsu Corp, while the second-ranking fixed charge holder was Denehurst, which were also the two shareholders in Metropolitan Collieries, he said.

"I'm currently in discussions and negotiations with them with a view to those two creditors ceding priority to the employees for their entitlements out of the proceeds from any sale proceeds," he said.
Kanematsu is a 10 percent shareholder in Metropolitan Colliery but is a secured creditor for A$20 million, he said.
Metropolitan Collieries appointed Price Waterhouse as administrators on following a significant disruption to production caused by a rock sill intrusion into the coal seam.
A company may be placed in administration when it can no longer pay its debts and the adminstrators then try to sell its assets on behalf of the creditors.
